new_statements.quote: Betonung. Die Betonung erfolgt mit wenigen Ausnahmen, die im Wortregister durch Akzente gekennzeichnet sind, auf der vorletzten Silbe. Hiebei sind auch die echten Diphthonge als zweisilbig anzusehen. Ausnahmen: lífaja Schmetterling, láhua Asche, búea Leguan, ámuni jener. Die enklitischen Possess.-Pronomina und das Pluralsuffix re haben keinen Einfluß auf die Betonung. Man sagt also: háta-re, íma-re, tína-ku.
new_statements.translation: Stress. With few exceptions, which are marked by accents in the word list, stress falls on the penultimate syllable. Here the true diphthongs are also to be counted as disyllabic. Exceptions: lífaja 'butterfly', láhua 'ash', búea 'monitor lizard', ámuni 'that one'. The enclitic possessive pronouns and the plural suffix re have no influence on the stress. Thus one says: háta-re, íma-re, tína-ku.
new_statements.citation: Tauern, Odo D. 1931. Beitrag zur Kenntnis der Sprachen und Dialekte von Seran (Schluss). Anthropos 26(1/2): 109-139 [section 'Die Wahinama-Sprache' = Manusela].
new_statements.locator: p.109, 'Lautlehre: Betonung' (p.125 of the archive.org Anthropos 26(1-2) scan)
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Quote check: opened (200 dpi render of p.125 = printed p.109 of, symlink ->) and read it by eye. Under 'Die Wahinama-Sprache' > 'Lautlehre' the paragraph reads exactly: 'Betonung. Die Betonung erfolgt mit wenigen Ausnahmen, die im Wortregister durch Akzente gekennzeichnet sind, auf der vorletzten Silbe. Hiebei sind auch die echten Diphthonge als zweisilbig anzusehen. Ausnahmen: lífaja Schmetterling, láhua Asche, búea Leguan, ámuni jener. Die enklitischen Possess.-Pronomina und das Pluralsuffix re haben keinen Einfluß auf die Betonung. Man sagt also: háta-re, íma-re, tína-ku.' -- verbatim as reported (the scanned text in garbles the accented forms, but the page scan is unambiguous). Surround…
new_statements.rule_in_words: In Wahinama/Manusela (the dialect cluster of which Huaulu is described as a member) stress is regularly on the penultimate syllable of the word/stem; a handful of lexical exceptions carry antepenultimate stress; enclitic possessive suffixes and plural -re are outside the stress domain, so stress stays on the stem penult (háta-re).
new_statements.exceptions: lífaja 'butterfly', láhua 'ash', búea 'monitor lizard', ámuni 'that' (antepenultimate); true diphthongs a͜i, a͜u count as two syllables for stress.
new_statements.domain_note: Statement is for Tauern's 'Wahinama' (= Manusela / Sou Upaa [wha], manu1258; data mainly from Manusela village), which Tauern says is spoken 'from the Wai Samal to the Sapolewa, from the high mountains to the north coast'. Huaulu [hud] is treated as a Manusela dialect by Loski & Loski 1989 and Collins 1983 but has its own ISO/Glottolog code; no statement specific to Huaulu was found. Word-level stress; enclitics (possessives, plural -re) do not shift it.
new_statements.identity_note: No description of Huaulu [hud] huau1237 itself was found (Glottolog 5.1: 0 descriptive refs; only Taber 1996 atlas, Loski & Loski 1989 and Taguchi 1989 surveys). The quoted stress statement is Tauern 1931 on 'Wahinama' = Manusela / Sou Upaa [wha], Glottolog manu1258 (data mainly from Manusela village), the other member of Glottolog's 'Manusela-Huaulu' node manu1263. Loski & Loski 1989:119-120 and Collins 1983:44 treat Huaulu as a Manusela dialect (Alakamat/Huaulu village; 64-72% lexical similarity with the other Manusela varieties per Loski & Loski's Table, reproduced in Grimes & Edwards 2026 Table 10.11), but ISO/Glottolog code it separately; using Tauern's rule for huau1237 would be a sister-lect proxy, hence not proposed for the catalog.

new_statements.quote: De spelling van Alfoersche woorden geschiedde klanknabootsend terwijl wordt opgemerkt, dat de klemtoon (op een zeer enkele uitzondering na) op de voorlaatste lettergreep valt. De e wordt ietwat kort, é geheel helder uitgesproken, terwijl e toonloos is.
new_statements.translation: The spelling of Alfur [indigenous Seramese] words was done phonetically, while it should be noted that the stress (with a very few exceptions) falls on the penultimate syllable. The e is pronounced somewhat short, é fully clear, while e [diacritic lost] is toneless.
new_statements.citation: Sachse, F. J. P. 1907. Het eiland Seran en zijne bewoners. Met een voorwoord van K. Martin. Leiden: E. J. Brill. [Voorrede: note on the spelling and stress of 'Alfoersche woorden'; Huaulu ('Hoaoeloe') treated pp.32-33, 82, 100-101, 110]
new_statements.locator: Voorrede (preface), sentence immediately preceding the acknowledgments 'Mijn oprechten en hartelijken dank breng ik hier aan den Hoogleeraar..'; second mention of 'klemtoon' in the main-text passage on which tribes 'eene bepaald verschillende taal spreken' (FTS page index 252)
new_statements.relation_note: Preface, on the transcription of native words: stress falls on the penultimate syllable with very few exceptions; e somewhat short, é clear, e-with-diacritic (lost in scanned) 'toonloos' (schwa). Main text adds that it would take close study to determine which tribes speak a really different language 'en welke slechts in uitdrukking, klemtoon en enkele woorden verschillen'. Seen only as consecutive, overlapping archive.org full-text-search fragments (archive.org download hosts could not be reached by automated download, 2 attempts); fragments.
new_statements.rule_in_words: For indigenous Seram ('Alfur') words generally, as transcribed by Sachse: penultimate stress with very few exceptions. Not a Huaulu-specific rule.
new_statements.exceptions: 'op een zeer enkele uitzondering na' (a very few exceptions), not listed in the fragments seen.
new_statements.identity_note: Ethnographic-administrative monograph on the whole island of Seram by the Dutch civil administrator at Wahai (North Seram). The stress remark is a blanket statement about the indigenous (Alfur) words cited in the book, i.e. about Seram languages in general as heard by the author, not about Huaulu [hud] or any single languoid; Huaulu (Hoaoeloe, Hoaoeloe-Alfoeren) figures in the narrative and index. Not in Glottolog's lists for huau1237/manu1258/manu1263.
